md_description: This DAG represents the generation and processing of single-cell amplified genomes from uncultured marine microbes collected from seawater, isolated by microfluidics, lysed, amplified by multiple displacement amplification, sequenced, assembled, annotated, and summarized in a metadata table. It captures the experimental methods and downstream assembly quality information needed to support exploration of microbial genomic diversity and ecological roles.

seawater_microbe_sample.reasoning: The seawater_microbe_sample node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic sample identity, origin, and environmental context that define what the sample is before any isolation or processing. I excluded isolation, lysis, amplification, sequencing, assembly, and quality fields because those belong to downstream Process/Capture/Derivative nodes. I also avoided duplicating generic experiment identifiers if they might already be generated at the root elsewhere; instead I focused on sample-specific provenance and seawater context needed to understand the starting material for SAG isolation.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the seawater microbial sample used as the starting material for single-cell isolation; use a stable string such as 'SWM-001'. This identifies the collected environmental sample itself, not an isolated cell or downstream SAG product.

Material class of the starting sample at collection time. For this node it should indicate seawater-derived microbial biomass or seawater with suspended uncultured microbes; capture once per sample before any cell isolation.
Date the seawater sample was collected from the environment before any processing. Record in ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD), e.g. '2026-05-14'.

Free-text or coded description of the seawater collection location, such as station name, transect, or geographic site. This identifies where the environmental sample originated and should not describe downstream processing locations.
Latitude of the seawater collection site in decimal degrees, measured or recorded at the time of sampling. Typical range -90 to 90; positive values north, negative values south.
Longitude of the seawater collection site in decimal degrees, measured or recorded at the time of sampling. Typical range -180 to 180; positive values east, negative values west.
Sampling depth of the seawater collection point in meters below the water surface, recorded at collection time. Use 0 for surface water; typical marine sampling range is 0 to several thousand meters.
In situ seawater temperature at the collection point, measured at sampling time in degrees Celsius. Typical marine range is approximately -2 to 40 depending on habitat.
In situ seawater salinity at the collection point, recorded at sampling time in practical salinity units (PSU). Typical oceanic range is about 0 to 40+ PSU depending on habitat.

Broad marine habitat or sampling context describing the source environment of the seawater sample, such as coastal surface water, open-ocean surface water, deep-sea water, or estuarine water. Record the context that characterizes the sample before cell isolation.

If the seawater sample was preprocessed before single-cell isolation, describe the concentration or filtration approach used to enrich microbial cells, such as filter pore size or centrifugation-based concentration. Record only the sample-preparation method, not the microfluidic isolation step.

Condition used to hold the seawater sample between collection and microfluidic isolation, such as temperature, darkness, or cryopreservation status. Record the state of the sample before isolation; do not include isolation or lysis parameters.

Optional free-text notes about the seawater sample that affect interpretation of the starting material, such as bloom status, turbidity, or visible debris. Use for sample-level provenance details not captured by the other fields.

microfluidic_single_cell_isolation.reasoning: The microfluidic_single_cell_isolation node is a Process, so I included fields only for how individual cells were isolated from the seawater sample: the microfluidic workflow, device/setup details, operating parameters, and an isolation success indicator. I excluded seawater sample provenance because that belongs to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded lysis, amplification, sequencing, assembly, and downstream quality metrics because those belong to later Process/Capture/Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating any generic sample identifiers that would have been defined elsewhere in the DAG.

md_schema.descr: Primary method used to isolate individual microbial cells from the seawater sample. For this node it should describe the microfluidic handling strategy used before downstream lysis, such as droplet-based sorting or microchannel capture.

Name of the microfluidic device or platform used for single-cell isolation, such as a commercial instrument or custom chip design. Record the platform used at the isolation step, not the sequencing instrument.
Version, revision, or build identifier of the microfluidic platform or chip used for cell isolation, if available. Use a string such as 'v2.1' or a chip revision code.
Geometry of the microfluidic capture structure used for isolation, such as channel width, trap design, or well arrangement. Include the design description relevant to cell capture efficiency.

Buffer composition used during microfluidic isolation of cells, including major salts, stabilizers, or surfactants if relevant. Describe the medium in which cells were handled during the isolation process.

Approximate concentration of cells loaded into the microfluidic isolation system, measured at the time of isolation in cells per milliliter. Typical values depend on enrichment strategy and should be recorded to support reproducibility.

Liquid flow rate used during microfluidic cell loading or sorting, measured in microliters per minute. Record the actively controlled rate during the isolation step; typical values depend on device design and may range from very low to moderate microfluidic flows.

Total duration of the microfluidic isolation operation in minutes, measured from start of loading until isolated cells were recovered for downstream lysis. Record the active isolation session time, not storage time.
How a single cell was obtained by the microfluidic system. This describes the operational capture mode used during isolation, such as one cell per trap or one cell per droplet.

Fraction of attempted captures that yielded an isolated single cell suitable for downstream lysis, reported as percent at the end of the isolation step. Use this as a process quality indicator for the isolation operation; typical values are 0 to 100.
Number of individual microbial cells successfully isolated from the seawater sample during this process step. Count the final recovered single cells available for downstream lysis.
Free-text notes on deviations, manual interventions, or unusual microfluidic events during isolation that could affect downstream SAG generation. Use for process-specific observations only.

isolated_single_cell.reasoning: The isolated_single_cell node is an Entity, so I included intrinsic properties of the physically isolated cell and its provenance from the isolation step, not the isolation process itself. I focused on identity, biological classification, morphological/phenotypic descriptors, and the immediate state of the cell prior to lysis. I excluded microfluidic settings, lysis, amplification, sequencing, and downstream genome quality because those belong to neighboring Process/Capture/Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating sample-level seawater metadata or generic experiment identifiers that would be handled elsewhere in the DAG.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the physically isolated individual cell selected for SAG generation; use a stable string such as 'cell_0001'. This identifies the isolated cell itself and should not be reused for the seawater sample or downstream DNA products.

Identifier of the upstream seawater sample from which this cell was isolated, linking the cell back to its environmental origin. Use the same sample identifier assigned at the Entity node for the starting material, e.g. 'SWM-001'.

Physical state of the cell immediately after microfluidic isolation and before lysis. Record whether the cell was intact, partially stressed, or otherwise recovered in a condition suitable for downstream lysis.

Microscopic morphology description of the isolated cell as observed after isolation and before lysis, such as coccoid, rod-shaped, filamentous, or pleomorphic. Use this field for visible phenotype only, not taxonomic identification.

Estimated diameter or longest dimension of the isolated cell measured or inferred at the isolation stage in micrometers. Typical microbial cell sizes are approximately 0.2 to 20 micrometers depending on taxon and shape.

Indicator of whether the isolated cell showed signs consistent with viability or membrane integrity at the time of isolation, based on the assay or observation used in this workflow. Record the observed status only if measured before lysis.

Lowest-confidence taxonomic assignment or broad lineage inferred for the isolated cell prior to genome generation, if any was made from microscopy or sorting context. Use a string such as 'Proteobacteria' or 'SAR11 clade' and keep this as provisional classification only.
Date and time when the cell was successfully isolated from the seawater sample and recovered for downstream lysis. Record in ISO 8601 format if available, such as '2026-05-14T10:35:00Z'.
Condition used to hold the isolated single cell before lysis, such as temperature, buffer, or incubation status. Record the post-isolation storage state of the entity, not the lysis protocol itself.

Optional free-text note describing any notable feature of the isolated cell, such as co-isolation concern, visible debris nearby, or manual selection rationale. Use only for cell-specific provenance details.

cell_lysis_process.reasoning: I corrected the lysis process schema to remove the colliding field operator_notes because that field name was already generated earlier in the DAG. I kept only lysis-specific process parameters and outcomes that remain within the semantic territory of cell lysis and do not duplicate upstream or downstream nodes. I also preserved the process-level distinction between how lysis was performed and any resulting DNA release outcome.

md_schema.descr: Primary lysis approach used to rupture the isolated single cell and release genomic DNA, such as chemical, enzymatic, thermal, mechanical, or combined lysis. Record the method applied at the lysis step, not the characteristics of the cell before lysis.
Composition of the buffer or reagent mix used during cell lysis, including major chemicals, salts, detergents, or enzymes if applicable. Describe the active lysis mixture used on the isolated cell.

Temperature at which lysis was performed, measured in degrees Celsius at the time of the lysis reaction. Typical values depend on the method and may range from ambient to elevated incubation temperatures.
Duration of the lysis incubation or treatment in minutes, measured from initiation of lysis until the cell was considered lysed or ready for downstream amplification. Record the active lysis time.
Total reaction volume used for lysis, measured in microliters. Record the volume of the lysis mixture in contact with the isolated cell.
Additional incubation condition during lysis, such as stationary, shaking, or heated hold. Use this to capture the physical handling condition applied while the lysis reaction proceeded.

Indicator of whether the cell lysis step successfully released DNA suitable for downstream amplification, recorded at the end of the lysis process. Use this as a process outcome flag for the lysis operation.

Qualitative assessment of lysis completeness or efficiency, based on microscopy, reaction outcome, or operator judgment after the lysis step. Use values or notes that describe whether lysis appeared complete, partial, or failed.
Optional rest time in minutes between completion of lysis and transfer to the downstream amplification step. Record only if the workflow includes a deliberate pause after lysis.

lysed_single_cell.reasoning: The lysed_single_cell node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic state of the cell after lysis and before amplification: that DNA has been released, the material state, and basic suitability for downstream MDA. I excluded lysis conditions because those belong to the upstream process, and I excluded amplification setup, sequencing, and assembly because those belong to downstream nodes. I also avoided the previously generated operator_notes field and any repeated sample or cell identifiers.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the lysed single-cell entity after lysis; use a stable string such as 'lysed_cell_0001'. This identifies the post-lysis material state of the cell and should not be reused for the pre-lysis cell or downstream DNA products.
Identifier of the upstream isolated single cell that was lysed to create this entity. Use the same cell identifier assigned at the isolated_single_cell node, e.g. 'cell_0001'.
Status of genomic DNA release after lysis, describing whether DNA was liberated from the cell into the reaction mixture. Record the post-lysis state of the entity before amplification.

Physical description of the post-lysis material, such as crude lysate, debris-containing lysate, or clarified lysate. Record the state of the sample immediately after lysis and before whole-genome amplification.
Approximate volume of the post-lysis lysate available for downstream amplification, measured in microliters. Record the volume after the lysis reaction is complete and before transfer to MDA.

Qualitative estimate of the integrity of released DNA in the lysate, based on observation or assay before amplification. Use this to capture whether DNA appeared intact, fragmented, or degraded prior to MDA.
Indicator that the lysed material was successfully prepared for downstream whole-genome amplification. This reflects readiness of the entity for the next process step, not the amplification itself.
Condition used to hold the lysed cell material before amplification, such as temperature or buffer status. Record the entity-level storage state between lysis and MDA.
Elapsed time in minutes between completion of lysis and initiation of downstream amplification. Record this as a post-lysis entity attribute relevant to preservation of released DNA.
Optional free-text notes about the lysed cell entity, such as visible debris, suspected contamination, or unusual appearance after lysis. Use for entity-specific observations only.

mda_amplification.reasoning: The mda_amplification node is a Process, so I included only how whole-genome amplification was performed: amplification chemistry, primer/polymerase system, reaction conditions, cycling/incubation parameters, duration, and a process success/quality indicator. I excluded properties of the lysed input entity and the amplified DNA output because those belong to upstream and downstream nodes, respectively. I also avoided any field names already generated in previous steps, including operator_notes, and kept software-related fields out because this process is wet-lab amplification rather than computational analysis.

md_schema.descr: Whole-genome amplification method used on the lysed single-cell DNA. For this node it should indicate multiple displacement amplification and any notable variant or implementation used before sequencing.
Name of the DNA polymerase used for multiple displacement amplification, such as phi29 or a vendor-specific equivalent. Record the active enzyme used during the amplification reaction.
Primer chemistry used to initiate multiple displacement amplification, such as random hexamers or proprietary MDA primers. Record the primer class used in the amplification reaction.
Total reaction volume for the MDA reaction, measured in microliters. Record the full amplification mixture volume at the start of the reaction.

Incubation temperature for MDA, measured in degrees Celsius during the amplification reaction. Typical phi29-based reactions are often performed near 30 C; record the actual temperature used in this workflow.
Total duration of the MDA reaction in hours, measured from reaction start until amplification was stopped. Record the active amplification time rather than any subsequent storage period.
Volume of lysed-cell material input into the MDA reaction, measured in microliters. Record the amount of lysate transferred into the amplification mixture at the start of the process.
Indicator of whether the MDA reaction produced sufficient amplified DNA for downstream sequencing. Record this process outcome at the end of amplification.

Approximate amount of amplified DNA recovered from the MDA reaction, measured in nanograms after completion of amplification. Use this as a process outcome metric for yield; typical single-cell MDA yields can vary widely.

Qualitative indicator of amplification bias or uneven coverage expected from the MDA reaction, based on operator assessment or QC before sequencing. Use this to record whether the amplification appeared uniform, biased, or poor.
Physical incubation mode used during MDA, such as stationary hold, heat block incubation, or gentle shaking. Record the actively controlled reaction handling condition.

sag_amplified_dna.reasoning: The sag_amplified_dna node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the amplified DNA material produced by MDA and its suitability for sequencing. I excluded amplification parameters because those belong to the upstream process, and I excluded sequencing settings, raw read properties, assembly, and annotation because those belong downstream. I also avoided reusing previously generated identifiers and the operator_notes field that was already flagged as a collision.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the amplified SAG DNA entity produced after MDA; use a stable string such as 'sag_dna_0001'. This identifies the post-amplification DNA material and should not be reused for the pre-amplification lysate or downstream read files.
Identifier of the lysed single-cell entity that served as the input to MDA. Use the same identifier assigned at the lysed_single_cell node, e.g. 'lysed_cell_0001'.

Status of the amplified DNA material after multiple displacement amplification, indicating whether it is ready for sequencing or requires further cleanup. Record the entity state immediately after amplification.

Measured concentration of the amplified DNA material after MDA, in nanograms per microliter. Record the concentration of the post-amplification entity prior to sequencing library preparation if applicable.
Total mass of amplified DNA recovered from the MDA product, measured in nanograms. This is an entity-level output measure recorded after amplification is complete.
Approximate size distribution or fragment profile of the amplified DNA entity, such as high-molecular-weight, smeared, or mixed size range. Record the observed DNA material profile before sequencing.
Indicator that the amplified DNA entity may contain obvious contamination or non-target DNA based on post-amplification checks. Record this as an entity-level quality flag before sequencing.
Condition used to store the amplified DNA before sequencing, such as temperature or buffer status. Record the storage state of the DNA entity between MDA and capture.
Volume of amplified DNA aliquot reserved for downstream sequencing, measured in microliters. Record the portion of the entity transferred to the sequencing capture step.

sag_sequencing_capture.reasoning: The sag_sequencing_capture node is a Capture node, so I included only the instrument configuration and actively controlled sequencing-session settings: platform identity, run chemistry, flow cell/lane configuration, read structure, run timing, and capture-level run quality indicators. I excluded sample and DNA material properties because those belong to upstream Entity nodes, and I excluded file properties and raw read dimensions because those belong to the downstream Signal node. I also avoided any previously generated field names, including operator_notes, and did not repeat software fields because this node represents wet-lab/instrument capture rather than computation.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the sequencing instrument used to sequence the amplified SAG DNA, such as Illumina, Thermo Fisher, or another vendor. Record the hardware manufacturer at the capture step.
Model name or instrument type of the sequencing system used for this SAG capture session, such as NovaSeq, MiSeq, NextSeq, or equivalent. Record the exact platform model configured for the run.
Serial number or instrument asset identifier for the sequencing platform used in this capture session, if tracked by the facility. Use a string identifier such as 'SN12345'.
Unique identifier for the sequencing run that generated the raw SAG reads; use a stable string such as 'RUN_2026_001'. This identifies the capture session itself, not the resulting data file.
Sequencing chemistry or kit used for the run, such as paired-end reagent kits or platform-specific chemistry version. Record the chemistry configured at the instrument capture step.

Type of flow cell or sequencing cartridge used during the capture session, such as patterned flow cell, standard flow cell, or specific lane configuration. Record the hardware consumable used for sequencing.
Configured read length in base pairs for the sequencing run, measured per read end at run setup. Typical values depend on platform and chemistry, such as 100, 150, or 250 bp.
Sequencing read structure used in this capture session. Record whether reads were generated as single-end or paired-end data.
Lane, channel, or equivalent partition used for the SAG sequencing capture, if the platform supports it. Record the run partition at which the DNA was sequenced.
Date and time when the sequencing run began for this SAG sample, recorded in ISO 8601 format if available, such as '2026-05-14T12:00:00Z'.
Date and time when the sequencing run completed for this SAG sample, recorded in ISO 8601 format if available. This marks the end of the capture session.
Instrument-level quality indicator for the sequencing session, such as pass, warning, or fail based on run metrics at completion. Use this as a capture-quality flag, not a raw-read quality measure.

raw_sag_reads.reasoning: The raw_sag_reads node is a Signal, so I kept only artifact-level properties of the raw sequencing data: file identity, file format, size, read count, total bases, pairing status, quality, adapter content, storage location, and basecalling provenance. I removed read_length_bp because it collided with a previously generated field in the DAG. I also excluded capture settings, assembly/annotation outputs, and any operator_notes-style process fields because those belong to other node types.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the raw sequencing reads artifact generated from the SAG sequencing capture; use a stable string such as 'reads_0001'. This identifies the file or dataset object, not the sequencing run.
Technical file format of the raw read data, such as FASTQ, BAM, or platform-specific archive format. Record the actual storage format of the signal artifact.
Size of the raw read file or file set in bytes, measured after sequencing and before any downstream processing. Use this as a technical artifact property.
Total number of reads contained in the raw sequencing artifact, counted after base calling and file generation. Record the raw read count for this signal dataset.
Total number of bases in the raw read dataset, measured in base pairs across all reads. This describes the size of the signal artifact before trimming or assembly.
Whether the raw reads are stored as single-end or paired-end data in the artifact. This describes the raw signal layout, not the capture configuration.
Mean Phred quality score across the raw read artifact, calculated over all bases or reads after base calling. Record this as a technical quality metric for the signal file.
Indicator of residual adapter sequence content in the raw reads, based on a post-sequencing technical check. Use this as a raw-data quality flag.
File path, URI, or storage location where the raw sequencing reads are stored, such as a local path or object-store URL. Record the artifact location after sequencing and before assembly.
Version of the basecalling software or instrument firmware that produced the raw read file, if tracked alongside the signal artifact. Record the technical generation version for the data file.

read_assembly.reasoning: The read_assembly node is a Process, so I included only how assembly was performed: assembler identity, version/source, key assembly parameters, preprocessing inputs to assembly, and process-level output quality indicators. I excluded raw read artifact properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded contig properties and assembly results because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided the previously generated read_length_bp field and other collisions such as operator_notes, keeping software details on this process node as required.

md_schema.descr: Name of the genome assembly software used to assemble raw SAG reads into draft contigs, such as SPAdes or another assembler. Record the software used at the assembly step.
Version of the assembly software used for the read assembly process, such as '3.15.5'. Record the exact version because assembly behavior can vary by release.

Repository, package source, or software distribution reference for the assembler used in this process, such as a GitHub URL, package name, or vendor distribution. Record where the assembly software was obtained.
Assembly mode or strategy used for this read assembly step, such as single-cell optimized assembly, isolate assembly, or meta-assembly. Record the configured operational mode for the assembler.
List or description of k-mer sizes used during assembly, if the assembler required k-mer selection. Record the key parameter set used for contig construction.
Minimum contig length threshold used by the assembler or post-assembly filtering, measured in base pairs. Record the cutoff applied during the assembly process.
Whether reads were trimmed, deduplicated, or otherwise filtered before assembly. Describe the preprocessing state of reads used as input to the assembly process.
Total runtime of the assembly process in minutes, measured from assembly start to completion. Record the operational duration of the computational assembly step.
Indicator that the assembly process completed successfully and produced a draft contig set suitable for downstream analysis. Use this as a process-level outcome flag.
Indicator that the assembly produced notable warnings or issues such as low coverage, fragmentation, or abnormal memory usage. Record this as a process-level QC flag for the assembly operation.

draft_sag_assembly.reasoning: The draft_sag_assembly node is a Derivative, so I included only computed output properties of the assembled contig set: assembly dimensions, contiguity statistics, sequence composition, and assembly-level quality indicators. I excluded assembler settings and runtime because those belong to the upstream read_assembly Process node, and I excluded raw read properties because those belong to the Signal node. I also avoided any previously generated field names, including read_length_bp and operator_notes, and focused on metrics a downstream user would need to assess and reuse the draft SAG assembly.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the draft SAG assembly object produced from read assembly; use a stable string such as 'assembly_0001'. This identifies the computed contig set, not the assembly software run.
Identifier of the raw SAG reads artifact used to create this draft assembly. Use the same identifier assigned to the raw_sag_reads node, e.g. 'reads_0001'.
Total number of contigs in the draft assembly, counted after assembly and any post-assembly filtering. Record this as an output dimension of the derivative genome assembly.
Total assembled sequence length in base pairs across all contigs in the draft SAG assembly. Record this as a computed output metric for the assembled genome.
Length of the largest contig in the draft assembly, measured in base pairs. This is a contiguity metric of the assembled genome output.
N50 contig length of the draft assembly, measured in base pairs. Typical values depend on genome completeness and fragmentation; record the standard assembly statistic derived from the contig set.
Percent GC content of the draft assembly, calculated over all assembled contigs after assembly completion. Use this as a composition metric for the derivative genome product.
Estimated sequencing coverage of the draft assembly, expressed as fold coverage (x). Record the coverage inferred for the assembled contig set after read mapping or equivalent estimation.
Qualitative assessment of how fragmented the draft assembly is after contig construction. Use this to summarize assembly contiguity for the derivative genome.
Indicator that the draft assembly may contain contaminant contigs or mixed-origin sequence based on downstream checks. Record this as an assembly-level quality flag.
Optional free-text notes about the assembled contig set, such as unusual fragmentation or unexpectedly small genome size. Use only for derivative-specific observations.

genome_annotation.reasoning: The genome_annotation node is a Process, so I included only how annotation was performed: annotation software identity and version, annotation database/source, key prediction settings, and a process-level outcome indicator. I excluded assembly statistics and contig properties because those belong to the upstream draft_sag_assembly Derivative, and I excluded predicted gene counts or functional results because those belong to the downstream annotated_sag_genome Derivative. I also avoided previously generated field names such as assembly_notes and any collisions across the DAG.

md_schema.descr: Name of the genome annotation software used to predict genes and functional features from the draft SAG assembly, such as Prokka, IMG/ER, or another tool. Record the software used at the annotation step.
Version of the annotation software used for this genome annotation process, such as '1.14.6'. Record the exact release because annotation behavior can vary by version.

Repository, package source, or distribution reference for the annotation software used in this process, such as a GitHub URL, package name, or vendor distribution. Record where the annotation tool was obtained.

Reference database or rule set used to support gene and function prediction during annotation, such as RefSeq, Pfam, KEGG, or a custom database. Record the primary resource used by the annotation pipeline.

Key parameter settings used by the genome annotation software, such as gene-calling thresholds, translation table, or minimum protein length. Record only the parameters that materially affect annotation output.
Genetic code table or translation table applied during annotation, if specified, such as bacterial/archaeal code. Record the code used for gene prediction in this process.
Total runtime of the genome annotation process in minutes, measured from annotation start to completion. Record the operational duration of the computational annotation step.
Indicator that the annotation process completed successfully and produced a usable feature set for the SAG assembly. Use this as a process-level outcome flag.
Indicator that the annotation produced notable warnings or issues, such as low-confidence gene calls or database mismatch. Record this as a process-level QC flag for annotation.

annotated_sag_genome.reasoning: The annotated_sag_genome node is a Derivative, so I included only computed annotation outputs and summary properties of the annotated genome product: identifier, gene and feature counts, functional category summaries, completeness of annotation output, and annotation-level quality flags. I excluded annotation software settings because those belong to the upstream genome_annotation Process node, and I excluded raw assembly metrics because those belong to the upstream draft_sag_assembly Derivative. I also avoided any previously generated field names such as annotation_warning_flag or assembly_notes, and I kept the fields centered on the annotated product rather than the computation that produced it.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the annotated SAG genome product; use a stable string such as 'annotated_genome_0001'. This identifies the computed annotation result, not the assembly or annotation software run.
Identifier of the draft SAG assembly used as input to annotation. Use the same identifier assigned to the draft_sag_assembly node, e.g. 'assembly_0001'.
Total number of predicted genes in the annotated SAG genome, counted after completion of annotation. Record the gene count as a derivative output metric.
Number of predicted tRNA features in the annotated genome product, counted after annotation. Use this as a summary feature count for the derivative genome.
Number of predicted rRNA features in the annotated genome product, counted after annotation. Record this as a summary feature count for the derivative genome.

Brief summary of major functional categories detected in the annotated genome, such as metabolism, transport, stress response, or ecological specialization. Record this as a high-level annotation summary rather than a software setting.
Percentage of predicted genes annotated as hypothetical proteins in the final genome product. Record this as a post-annotation summary statistic, typically ranging from 0 to 100 percent.

Qualitative indicator of how complete the annotation output appears for this genome, based on feature recovery and consistency. Use this as a derivative-level quality assessment, not a software QC flag.
Indicator that the annotated genome contains suspiciously redundant or overlapping functional assignments after annotation. Record this as a derivative-level quality flag.

Optional free-text notes on the annotated genome product, such as unusual gene content, strong enrichment for a pathway, or sparse functional annotation. Use only for derivative-specific observations.

quality_metric_computation.reasoning: The quality_metric_computation node is a Process, so I included only how the QC metrics were computed: analysis software identity and version, input sources, metric definitions or thresholds, and process-level status. I excluded assembly and annotation results themselves because those belong to upstream Derivative nodes, and I excluded the computed completeness/contamination values because those belong to the downstream assembly_qc_metrics Derivative. I also avoided previously generated field names such as annotated_genome_notes and kept software details on this process node as required.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or pipeline used to compute assembly and annotation quality metrics, such as CheckM or another QC tool. Record the computational tool used for this metric-computation process.
Version of the QC analysis software or pipeline used to compute completeness, contamination, and related metrics. Record the exact version because metric calculations can vary by release.
Repository, package source, or distribution reference for the QC software used in this process, such as a GitHub URL, package name, or vendor distribution. Record where the QC tool was obtained.
Identifier of the draft SAG assembly used as one input to quality metric computation. Use the same identifier assigned to the draft_sag_assembly node, e.g. 'assembly_0001'.
Identifier of the annotated SAG genome used as one input to quality metric computation. Use the same identifier assigned to the annotated_sag_genome node, e.g. 'annotated_genome_0001'.
Key thresholds or classification cutoffs used when computing quality metrics, such as completeness or contamination decision boundaries. Record the criteria applied by the QC process.
Total runtime of the quality metric computation process in minutes, measured from analysis start to completion. Record the operational duration of the QC computation step.
Indicator that the quality metric computation completed successfully and produced a usable set of metrics. Use this as a process-level outcome flag.
Indicator that the QC computation produced warnings or limitations, such as insufficient marker genes or weak signal from the draft assembly. Record this as a process-level flag.

assembly_qc_metrics.reasoning: The assembly_qc_metrics node is a Derivative, so I kept only computed QC outputs and final assessment fields for the derived metrics object. I removed the collided source_draft_assembly_id field and avoided any other previously generated identifiers or notes fields. The remaining fields describe the QC result itself—completeness, contamination, heterogeneity, marker recovery, and classification—without re-describing upstream assembly or annotation products.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed assembly QC metrics object; use a stable string such as 'qc_0001'. This identifies the derived metrics record, not the QC software run.
Identifier of the annotated SAG genome used to compute these QC metrics. Use the same identifier assigned to the annotated_sag_genome node, e.g. 'annotated_genome_0001'.

Estimated genome completeness reported by the QC computation, expressed as percent. Record the completeness value derived from the draft assembly and annotation outputs; typical values range from 0 to 100 percent.

Estimated genome contamination reported by the QC computation, expressed as percent. Record the contamination value derived from the QC analysis; typical values range from 0 upward, with lower values preferred.
Estimated strain heterogeneity or mixed-strain signal reported by the QC computation, expressed as percent when available. Record this derived metric if the QC workflow calculates it.
Percent of expected marker genes recovered by the QC process, if computed. Record this as a derived assembly quality statistic used to interpret completeness.

Overall quality classification assigned to the assembly based on computed metrics. Use this as the final derivative-level assessment of whether the SAG assembly is high-quality, medium-quality, or poor-quality.
Indicator that the assembly QC metrics meet the study's acceptance criteria for downstream use. Record this final pass/fail decision as a derivative-level flag.
Optional free-text notes describing noteworthy aspects of the computed QC metrics, such as borderline completeness or unexpectedly high contamination. Use only for derivative-level observations.

metadata_table_generation.reasoning: The metadata_table_generation node is a Process, so I included only how the final table was assembled: table format, schema/version, source inputs, row and column layout, export format, and generation status. I excluded sample, cell, sequencing, assembly, annotation, and QC values themselves because those belong to upstream Entity/Signal/Derivative nodes that are being consolidated, not to the table-generation process. I also avoided any previously generated field names, including source_draft_assembly_id and operator_notes, and kept software/analysis details on this process node as required.

md_schema.descr: Structured format used to consolidate SAG methods descriptions and quality metrics into the final metadata table, such as CSV, TSV, Excel workbook, or database table. Record the table format produced by this process.
Version or release identifier of the metadata table schema used for this consolidation step, such as 'v1.0'. Record the schema version that defines the final table structure.
Granularity of rows in the final metadata table, such as one row per SAG, one row per cell, or one row per sample. Record the unit of tabulation established by this process.
Total number of columns in the final metadata table after consolidation, counted at completion of this process. Record the final table width as a process output characteristic.
Number of records or rows written into the final metadata table, counted after generation is complete. Record the total number of entries exported by this process.

High-level list or description of the upstream metadata objects merged into the final table, such as isolation methods, sequencing metrics, assembly QC, and annotation summaries. Record the contributing source categories rather than their detailed values.
File path, URI, or database location where the final metadata table was written. Record the storage location produced by the table-generation process.
Name of the software, script, or workflow component used to assemble the final metadata table. Record the tool used to perform the table consolidation.
Version of the table-generation software or pipeline used for this process, such as a script release or package version. Record the exact version because output formatting may vary by release.
Indicator that the metadata table generation completed successfully and produced a usable final table. Use this as a process-level outcome flag.

sag_metadata_table.reasoning: The sag_metadata_table node is a Derivative, so I kept only artifact-level properties of the final consolidated table and removed any fields that collided with earlier DAG steps, including metadata_table_format, metadata_table_column_count, and metadata_table_schema_version. I also excluded the biological and process details already represented upstream, since this node should describe the final reusable table artifact itself. The remaining fields focus on table identity, size, row count, completeness/validation, storage location, and notes without repeating earlier generated names.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the final SAG metadata table artifact; use a stable string such as 'sag_meta_0001'. This identifies the table itself, not the process that generated it.
Size of the final metadata table artifact in bytes, measured after table generation is complete. This is a technical property of the output file or table export.
Number of rows in the final SAG metadata table, counted after all records have been consolidated. Record the final table length as an artifact-level property.

Indicator that the final table contains the expected consolidated fields for isolation, lysis, amplification, sequencing, assembly, annotation, and quality information. Use this as a table-level completeness check.
Result of any validation performed on the final metadata table artifact, such as pass, warning, or fail after schema checks and record integrity checks. Record the artifact-level validation status.
File path, URI, or database location where the final metadata table artifact is stored. Record the artifact location for downstream access.
Optional free-text notes about the final metadata table artifact, such as formatting quirks, missing optional fields, or export caveats. Use only for artifact-specific observations.
